questions.title: Partial Yamanaka Reprogramming: Decoupling Epigenetic Rejuvenation from Oncogenic Teratoma Formation
questions.brief: Investigate transient cellular reprogramming to reverse biological age without loss of cell identity. (1) Model the kinetics of cyclic or transient Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 (OSK, omitting c-Myc to suppress oncogenesis) delivery via inducible promoters or mRNA-LNPs. (2) Formulate the critical time window: quantify how Horvath DNA methylation clocks and transcriptomic aging signatures revert during early reprogramming (Days 2-6) before cells lose lineage-specific chromatin architecture and enter the dangerous pluripotent/teratoma phase (Day 8+). (3) Model chromatin accessibility dynamics (ATAC-seq/ChIP-seq peaks) and heterochromatin markers (H3K9me3, HP1) restoration.
groundTruth: Sarkar et al. (2020) and Lu et al. (2020 Nature) demonstrated that OSK expression in mammalian retinal ganglion cells restores visual function and reverses Horvath DNA methylation age
Continuous unconstrained Yamanaka factor expression in vivo causes lethal teratomas and multi-organ dysgenesis within weeks
Omission of the c-Myc oncogene (using OSK instead of OSKM) substantially reduces neoplastic transformation while retaining epigenetic rejuvenation capacity
The epigenetic clock (Horvath pan-tissue clock) tracks DNA methylation at specific CpG sites, measuring biological as opposed to chronological age
Short cyclic bursts (e.g., 2 days on, 5 days off) preserve somatic cellular identity while resetting epigenetic noise
questions.deliverable: A Python computational engine `epigenetic_reprogramming_engine.py` with test suite and a scientific monograph `EPIGENETIC_REPROGRAMMING_AND_TERATOMA_BOUNDARIES.md` quantifying the safe temporal rejuvenation window.

questions.title: Targeted Senolysis: BCL-2/BCL-xL Dependencies, SASP Secretome Shutdown, and Toxicity Boundaries
questions.brief: Investigate the selective elimination of senescent cells and neutralization of the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP). (1) Model senescent cell anti-apoptotic pathways (SCAPs): dependency on BCL-2, BCL-xL, and BCL-W family proteins, and the p53-p21-p16^INK4a checkpoint axes. (2) Quantify the therapeutic window and toxicity trade-offs: contrast broad BCL-xL inhibitors (Navitoclax/ABT-263), which cause dose-limiting thrombocytopenia due to platelet BCL-xL dependence, with targeted senolytics (Dasatinib + Quercetin, Fisetin) and galactose-conjugated/senolytic prodrugs (SSK1). (3) Model the paracrine spread of senescence driven by SASP factors (IL-6, IL-8, TGF-beta, MMPs) and quantify tissue rejuvenation post-senolytic clearance.
groundTruth: Senescent cells accumulate with age in tissues, permanently arresting the cell cycle via p16^INK4a and p21^CIP1 while resisting apoptosis
The Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP) secretes pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1beta) and metalloproteinases that induce paracrine senescence in neighboring healthy cells
Navitoclax (ABT-263) selectively kills senescent cells by inhibiting BCL-2 and BCL-xL, but is clinically dose-limited by severe on-target platelet thrombocytopenia
Platelet survival is obligately dependent on BCL-xL to restrain Bak-mediated apoptosis (Mason et al. 2007)
Intermittent 'hit-and-run' senolytic dosing is effective because senescent cells take weeks to re-accumulate, avoiding the toxicity of continuous daily administration
questions.deliverable: A Python computational engine `senolytic_pharmacodynamics_engine.py` with test suite and a scientific monograph `SENOLYTIC_TARGETING_AND_SASP_ELIMINATION.md`.

questions.title: The Telomere-p53-Mitochondrial Axis: TERT Regulation, ROS Cascades, and Stem Cell Exhaustion
questions.brief: Investigate the molecular coupling between telomere attrition, DNA damage responses, and mitochondrial metabolic collapse. (1) Model the core cascade: critical telomere shortening triggers persistent DNA damage response (DDR) at chromosome ends (gamma-H2AX, 53BP1 foci), activating p53. (2) Formulate p53-mediated repression of PGC-1alpha and PGC-1beta, driving mitochondrial dysfunction, electron transport chain (ETC) decoupling, and increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) leakage. (3) Model the feedback loop where mitochondrial ROS induces further oxidative 8-oxoguanine damage preferentially at G-rich telomeric repeats. (4) Quantify gene therapy rescue via adeno-associated virus (AAV)-delivered TERT versus oncogenic immortalization risks.
groundTruth: Sahin et al. (2011 Nature) proved that telomere dysfunction represses PGC-1alpha and PGC-1beta via p53, directly driving mitochondrial failure and metabolic compromise
Telomeres consist of tandem TTAGGG repeats that are uniquely vulnerable to single-strand oxidative damage due to high guanine triplet content
Human somatic cells lack sufficient telomerase activity due to transcriptional repression of the TERT catalytic subunit, leading to the Hayflick limit of ~50 population doublings
AAV-mediated telomerase (TERT) gene therapy in adult mice extends median lifespan by 13-24% without increasing cancer incidence (Bernardes de Jesus et al. 2012)
Over 85-90% of human cancers reactivate TERT via promoter mutations (C228T, C250T) or gene amplification to achieve replicative immortality
questions.deliverable: A Python computational engine `telomere_mitochondrial_axis_engine.py` with test suite and a scientific monograph `TELOMERE_P53_MITOCHONDRIAL_AXIS_ANALYSIS.md`.

questions.title: Nutrient-Sensing Longevity Networks: Intermittent mTORC1 Inhibition, Autophagy, and AMPK Activation
questions.brief: Investigate the evolutionary conserved nutrient-sensing signaling network governing lifespan extension. (1) Formulate the dual mTOR complexes: rapamycin-sensitive mTORC1 (Raptor-driven protein synthesis, S6K1, 4E-BP1, autophagy inhibition via ULK1 phosphorylation) versus mTORC2 (Rictor-driven, essential for Akt Ser473 phosphorylation, insulin sensitivity, and immune function). (2) Model the kinetics of intermittent vs chronic rapamycin administration: why chronic dosing disrupts mTORC2 assembly, causing glucose intolerance and immunosuppression, whereas intermittent dosing preserves mTORC2 while periodically purging cellular debris via autophagy. (3) Integrate AMPK and Sirtuin (SIRT1/SIRT3) activation: NAD+ depletion kinetics with age (CD38 upregulation and NAMPT decline) and caloric restriction mimetics (metformin, spermidine).
groundTruth: Rapamycin is the only pharmacological agent proven to consistently extend both median and maximum lifespan across multiple mammalian model species in the NIA Interventions Testing Program (ITP)
mTORC1 directly inhibits autophagy by phosphorylating ULK1 at Ser757, preventing ULK1-AMPK interaction
Chronic continuous rapamycin treatment sequesters free mTOR from assembling into mTORC2, leading to peripheral insulin resistance and impaired immune response (Lamming et al. 2012 Science)
NAD+ levels decline by up to 50% in aged tissues, driven in part by increased activity of the NADase CD38 in pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages (Camacho-Pereira et al. 2016)
Intermittent or low-dose rapamycin regimens maximize the mTORC1-to-mTORC2 selectivity ratio, extending healthspan without metabolic toxicity
questions.deliverable: A Python computational engine `nutrient_sensing_longevity_engine.py` with test suite and a scientific monograph `NUTRIENT_SENSING_NETWORKS_AND_MTOR_KINETICS.md`.
